name: Scriba
description: Warm cream paper, ink-black type, one burnt-orange accent. Calm, clever, hand-drawn. The Egyptian scribe cat explains things.
mascotDescription: a sleek Egyptian cat scribe in profile, thick black single-weight ink outline, Eye of Horus marking around the eye, patterned collar with spiral motifs, holding a burnt-orange pen, no fill colour except the orange pen
imageStyle: Minimal hand-drawn editorial illustration: thick uniform black ink outlines (like a bold felt-tip line drawing), flat warm cream paper background (#FBF4EA), almost no shading, a single burnt-orange accent colour (#C1602E) used sparingly, subtle ancient-Egyptian scribe motifs (papyrus, hieroglyph-like ornaments) where it fits, generous empty space, centred subject, no gradients, no photorealism, no text or letters.
bible:
Voice: a wise, slightly witty study companion, never shouty. Short sentences. One idea per scene.
Layout: lots of cream space, ink text, orange only for the 1-2 words that matter (*word*). Prefer Title, BigStat, Bullets, Quote over full-bleed photos; images are line illustrations shown with Card or as a centred illustration, not ImageBG.
Mascot: the cat appears in the hook (pos='peek' or 'center') and the CTA, and at most once in the middle. Use <Mascot /> with the base image or a pose generated with --mascot.
Never: neon colours, dark backgrounds, stock-photo looks, all-caps shouting captions, emoji overload (max one Icon per reel).
